name: Sirloin Steak with Basil Compound Butter, Roasted Potatoes & Snap Peas
ingredients: 1 ½ lb striploin (New York strip) steak
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil.
Cut butter into small pieces, place in a small bowl, and set aside to soften.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.

Slice potatoes crosswise into ¼-inch thick rounds. Transfer to the baking sheet, season with spices, and spread out in a single layer; dot potatoes with ⅓ of the butter. (Reserve remaining butter for later.)
Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, tossing halfway through, until the potatoes are fork-tender and golden, about 25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, zest lemon into the bowl with the remaining butter. Cut lemon into wedges and set aside for serving.
Peel and mince garlic; add to the bowl with the butter.

Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons; add to the bowl. Mash the butter, garlic, and basil together with the back of a spoon until smooth. Set the compound butter aside.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat the steak dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.

Once the skillet is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook until desired doneness, 2-5 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate, loosely cover with aluminum foil, and set aside to rest.
Return the skillet to medium-high heat. Add more butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add snap peas, salt, and pepper; stir-fry until the peas are fork-tender, about 4 minutes.
Thinly slice steak against the grain.
To serve, divide roasted potatoes, steak, and snap peas between plates. Top steak with compound butter and squeeze lemon over the peas. Enjoy!
author: Mealime
